assumptions: no observed dataset, benchmark, or expert-judgment input was supplied; all values are heuristic priors
this subdomain is a node in a knowledge-searcher meta-KB about where and how to find, evaluate, and trust authoritative scholarly sources
scope is the publication/dissemination system and source provenance, not manuscript writing craft or statistical analysis internals
venue, funder, and policy specifics vary by discipline and over time and must be revalidated against current sources
exclusions: manuscript writing and argumentation craft (covered by research-craft KBs)
citation-impact metric computation internals (covered by bibliometrics KBs)
full-text retrieval ranking algorithm internals (covered by IR KBs)
statistical analysis and study execution internals

competency_questions.question: What artifact type and publication intent (find vs disseminate) scope this work?
Which open-access route (gold/green/diamond/hybrid/closed) and venue class fit the mandates and budget?
What is the total cost of dissemination including APCs, waivers, and agreements?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer cites APC_ECON and PREPRINT outputs

competency_questions.question: Which peer-review model and editorial workflow apply, and what bias/timing tradeoffs follow?
When should a registered report, megajournal, or overlay journal be used instead of a standard journal?
How are preprint and version-of-record relationships tracked across versions?
Which version should be cited or deposited, and what is its post-publication status?
Which license and reuse rights apply to the article and its data/software?
What rights-retention and embargo/deposit plan satisfies the funder mandate?
Is the venue legitimate and non-predatory, and are all mandates met?
What is the overall provenance-and-trust judgment for a given source?
Is the artifact discoverable and machine-retrievable via indexing and persistent identifiers?
Who are the legitimate authors/contributors and are conflicts of interest disclosed?
What auditable decision record captures route, venue, license, provenance, and compliance?

glossary.definition: the final published, citable version of an article hosted by the publisher
author-formatted manuscript after peer acceptance but before publisher copyediting
a manuscript shared publicly before formal peer review
immediate OA at the publisher, often funded by an APC
OA via author self-archiving of a permitted version in a repository
OA with no APC to authors and no paywall to readers
article processing charge paid to make an article openly available
a venue charging fees while lacking genuine editorial and peer-review services
article format granting in-principle acceptance on the protocol before results
large-scale journal reviewing for soundness rather than significance
journal that curates and peer-reviews articles hosted on a preprint server
author strategy to keep copyright/reuse rights despite a publisher agreement
standardized public licenses (CC BY, CC BY-NC, CC0) governing reuse
the documented origin, version lineage, and trust signals of a scholarly source

evidence_label_policy.rule: all values are heuristic priors; observed and experimentally_validated labels are disallowed without supplied data

source_registry.description: model heuristic priors for scholarly publication system planning, evaluation, and provenance assessment

nodes.definition: Define the publishing question: artifact type (article, preprint, dataset, registered report), target audience, discipline norms, and the find/evaluate purpose this node serves.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: audience, discipline, or artifact type is restated by the user

pros.claim: clarifies which venue/route applies before any retrieval or evaluation
pros.example: choosing preprint+journal vs journal-only changes search strategy for a bioRxiv-mirrored article

cons.claim: over-narrow scoping can exclude valid grey/preprint sources
cons.example: scoping to peer-reviewed-only drops a key arXiv result

nodes.definition: Select the publication route (gold, green, diamond, hybrid OA, or closed) and concrete venue class given discipline norms, funder mandates, and budget.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a funder mandate or budget envelope changes

pros.claim: aligns route with mandate and budget before submission, avoiding rework
pros.example: picking a diamond OA venue satisfies a Plan S mandate at zero APC

cons.claim: route choice interacts with embargo, license, and APC, raising coupling
cons.example: green route chosen but publisher embargo blocks deposit timing

nodes.definition: Characterize and choose among peer-review models (single-blind, double-blind, open, post-publication, registered reports) and their bias, transparency, and timing tradeoffs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: venue review-model policy or integrity requirements change

pros.claim: matches review model to integrity and transparency goals
pros.example: registered-report pre-registration curbs HARKing for a confirmatory study

cons.claim: model choice trades reviewer anonymity against accountability
cons.example: open review deters early-career reviewers from candid critique

nodes.definition: Design Stage-1 registered-report or pre-registration content so in-principle acceptance precedes results, controlling outcome-dependent publication decisions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: study protocol or analysis plan is amended

pros.claim: decouples acceptance from results, reducing publication bias
pros.example: IPA granted before data collection removes pressure to find significance

cons.claim: rigid protocols can impede legitimate exploratory follow-up
cons.example: a locked analysis plan blocks a justified post-hoc subgroup test

nodes.definition: Decide preprint posting, server choice (arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv, SSRN), versioning, and the relationship of the preprint to the eventual version of record.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: journal or server preprint policy changes

pros.claim: establishes priority and open access fast, before formal review
pros.example: a bioRxiv preprint timestamps a discovery months before journal acceptance

cons.claim: preprints are unreviewed and can be miscited as validated
cons.example: a preprint with a later-retracted claim spreads via media

nodes.definition: Distinguish and track preprint, submitted, accepted manuscript (AAM), and version of record (VoR), including DOIs, version relations, and which version to cite or deposit.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new version, correction, or retraction is issued

pros.claim: prevents citing or depositing the wrong version
pros.example: ensuring the VoR DOI, not the preprint DOI, anchors the formal citation

cons.claim: version proliferation confuses retrieval and provenance
cons.example: three coexisting versions cause inconsistent metadata across indexes

nodes.definition: Choose and apply the correct license (Creative Commons variants, all-rights-reserved) and reconcile it with reuse, funder, and venue requirements.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a funder or venue license requirement changes

pros.claim: a clear CC license enables compliant reuse and text mining
pros.example: CC BY lets a meta-analysis legally redistribute extracted figures

cons.claim: incompatible licenses block deposit or downstream reuse
cons.example: CC BY-NC blocks commercial reuse a funder mandate requires CC BY

nodes.definition: Manage copyright assignment vs retention, rights-retention strategies (e.g., prior-license addenda), and author-publisher agreements affecting deposit and reuse.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a publisher agreement or funder rights policy changes

pros.claim: rights retention preserves author reuse and green-deposit options
pros.example: a rights-retention addendum lets an author self-archive the AAM immediately

cons.claim: signing away copyright can permanently block compliant deposit
cons.example: full transfer with embargo prevents satisfying an immediate-OA mandate

nodes.definition: Analyze journal business models and article processing charges (APCs), transformative/read-and-publish agreements, waivers, and total cost of dissemination.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an institutional agreement or APC price changes

pros.claim: surfaces hidden costs and waivers before commitment
pros.example: an institutional read-and-publish deal zeroes an otherwise large APC

cons.claim: APC focus can bias choice toward paywalled prestige over fit
cons.example: chasing a high-APC hybrid journal when a diamond venue fits better

nodes.definition: Vet a venue for legitimacy and quality using indexing, transparency, peer-review evidence, and predatory-journal warning signs before submission or citation trust.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a venue is delisted, acquired, or shows new predatory signals

pros.claim: blocks submission to or citation of illegitimate venues
pros.example: DOAJ plus COPE membership checks flag a deceptive lookalike journal

cons.claim: crude blocklists misjudge legitimate new or regional venues
cons.example: a valid Global-South diamond journal flagged as predatory by a stale list

nodes.definition: Ensure the published artifact is indexed and discoverable across databases, indexes, and discovery layers via persistent identifiers and metadata coverage.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an index changes coverage or a PID stops resolving

pros.claim: makes the artifact findable in the systems searchers actually use
pros.example: Scopus plus DOAJ indexing ensures the article appears in systematic-review searches

cons.claim: over-trusting one index hides coverage gaps
cons.example: relying only on Web of Science misses a regionally indexed venue

nodes.definition: Assign and validate persistent identifiers (DOI, ORCID, ROR, funder IDs) and structured publication metadata that anchor provenance and machine retrieval.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a metadata schema or PID registration changes

pros.claim: PIDs and rich metadata enable reliable machine retrieval and linkage
pros.example: ORCID plus ROR let a system disambiguate authors and affiliations automatically

cons.claim: incomplete or wrong metadata silently degrades findability
cons.example: a missing funder ID breaks compliance reporting and discovery

nodes.definition: Model the editorial and production pipeline (submission, triage, review assignment, revision, copyediting, typesetting, publication) and its handoff gates.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an editorial or production policy changes

pros.claim: makes the path from submission to VoR explicit and auditable
pros.example: tracking triage-to-decision timing reveals a reviewer-assignment bottleneck

cons.claim: opaque workflows hide delays and conflict-of-interest gaps
cons.example: an unlogged editor handling reduces COI accountability

nodes.definition: Assess megajournal (soundness-not-significance) and overlay-journal (curation over preprint servers) models for fit, cost, and trust implications.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a megajournal or overlay-journal policy changes

pros.claim: captures newer venue forms that change selectivity and cost
pros.example: an overlay journal adds peer review atop an arXiv preprint at minimal cost

cons.claim: soundness-only review can be mistaken for significance vetting
cons.example: a megajournal acceptance read as a strong-novelty signal it does not provide

nodes.definition: Manage embargo periods and green-route self-archiving: which version, where, and when deposit is permitted to satisfy open-access mandates.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an embargo or mandate deadline changes

pros.claim: times deposit to satisfy mandates without violating embargo
pros.example: depositing the AAM after a 6-month embargo meets an after-embargo policy

cons.claim: missed embargo timing causes non-compliance or takedown
cons.example: early VoR deposit triggers a publisher takedown notice

nodes.definition: Handle the post-publication integrity record: corrections, expressions of concern, retractions, and their propagation to indexes and citing works.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a correction, concern, or retraction is issued or updated

pros.claim: ensures retraction status is detected and honored downstream
pros.example: catching a Retraction-Watch flag prevents citing a retracted trial as evidence

cons.claim: slow propagation lets retracted work keep being cited
cons.example: an index lag means a retracted paper still surfaces as valid for months

nodes.definition: Publish and cite associated data and software artifacts as first-class outputs with FAIR principles, data DOIs, and repository deposit (per Borgman).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a data-sharing policy or repository status changes

pros.claim: makes data/software citable and reusable alongside the article
pros.example: a Zenodo-deposited dataset with a DOI lets reuse be tracked and credited

cons.claim: data availability statements without real access mislead
cons.example: a data-available-on-request statement that never yields data

nodes.definition: Define authorship, contributor roles (CRediT), and credit attribution policies, including affiliation and conflict-of-interest disclosure.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a contributor or conflict-of-interest fact changes

pros.claim: prevents authorship disputes and clarifies accountability
pros.example: CRediT roles make a large-collaboration contribution map auditable

cons.claim: honorary or ghost authorship distorts credit and accountability
cons.example: a gift authorship inflates a senior figure apparent output

nodes.definition: Synthesize venue legitimacy, version, review model, retraction status, and identifiers into a provenance-and-trust judgment for a given source.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any constituent trust signal (venue, version, retraction, review) changes

pros.claim: integrates scattered trust signals into one defensible judgment
pros.example: combining DOAJ status, VoR, and no-retraction yields a high-trust source decision

cons.claim: aggregating weak signals can produce false confidence
cons.example: a legitimate-venue paper trusted despite an unnoticed expression of concern

nodes.definition: Track and verify compliance with funder, institutional, and national open-access and data mandates across the publication lifecycle.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a funder or institutional mandate is added or revised

pros.claim: verifies every mandate is met before and after publication
pros.example: confirming license, deposit, and reporting satisfies a Plan S obligation

cons.claim: partial compliance can void funding or trigger penalties
cons.example: a met license but missed deposit deadline breaches the full mandate

nodes.definition: Compile the route, venue, license, version, cost, provenance, and compliance decisions into a reusable, auditable publication/evaluation decision record.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any upstream decision (route, venue, license, provenance, compliance) changes

pros.claim: turns scattered decisions into one auditable, reusable record
pros.example: a single decision record lets a reviewer reconstruct why a venue was trusted

cons.claim: premature synthesis locks in unvalidated upstream decisions
cons.example: compiling the record before provenance is validated propagates an error

edges.why_related: route selection requires the scoped artifact type and intent
review model is conditioned on the chosen venue/route
registered-report design presumes a registered-report-capable model
edges.risk_of_conflict: designing RR for a non-RR venue wastes effort
edges.resolution_rule: confirm model supports RR before designing

edges.why_related: preprint decision depends on route and venue preprint policy
version control requires the preprint to exist in the lineage
edges.example: preprint DOI feeds the lineage map
edges.resolution_rule: preprint must be registered before lineage closure

edges.why_related: license choice is bounded by route and venue license options
edges.risk_of_conflict: route may force a restrictive license
edges.example: gold route may mandate CC BY

edges.why_related: rights retention strategy is set against the chosen license
edges.example: CC BY plus addendum preserves reuse

edges.why_related: deposit/embargo plan depends on retained rights
cost analysis depends on the chosen route business model
edges.resolution_rule: route business model dominates cost analysis

edges.why_related: venue vetting operates on the route candidate venues
provenance judgment requires the venue legitimacy assessment
edges.benefit_of_coupling: legitimacy is a core trust signal
edges.resolution_rule: legitimacy must be assessed before provenance

edges.why_related: provenance requires a resolved version lineage
provenance must incorporate post-publication status
review model evidence informs the provenance judgment
edges.risk_of_conflict: unknown review model lowers trust certainty

edges.why_related: indexing checks operate on resolved version metadata
edges.benefit_of_coupling: version map targets correct index records
edges.risk_of_conflict: indexing the wrong version misleads discovery

edges.why_related: indexing coverage check uses the vetted venue index status
edges.resolution_rule: vet venue before trusting index claims

edges.why_related: identifiers and metadata attach to specific versions
edges.benefit_of_coupling: version map defines which PIDs apply

edges.why_related: editorial workflow instantiates the chosen review model
megajournal/overlay forms constrain how the review model applies
overlay journals require an underlying preprint
data/software publishing inherits or adapts the license decision
edges.example: CC0 for data, CC BY for text
edges.resolution_rule: resolve license before data artifact licensing

edges.why_related: data artifacts need persistent identifiers and metadata
authorship policy follows from the scoped contributor context
edges.benefit_of_coupling: scope frames who counts as author

edges.why_related: post-publication status updates attach to the version lineage
edges.benefit_of_coupling: version map locates the corrected/retracted record
edges.risk_of_conflict: status applied to wrong version misleads
edges.example: retraction notice tied to the VoR
edges.resolution_rule: resolve version before recording post-pub status

edges.why_related: compliance verification consumes the license decision
edges.example: CC BY satisfies a Plan S clause

edges.why_related: compliance includes cost/agreement mandate components
compliance verifies deposit/embargo mandate satisfaction
edges.benefit_of_coupling: deposit plan is a mandate component

edges.why_related: the decision record requires the route decision
edges.benefit_of_coupling: route is a core recorded decision

edges.why_related: the decision record requires the venue legitimacy assessment
the decision record requires the license decision
the decision record requires the provenance/trust judgment
edges.benefit_of_coupling: provenance is the trust core of the record

edges.why_related: the decision record requires the compliance status
cost minimization pressures route choice against open-access preference
edges.risk_of_conflict: cheap closed route undermines OA goals
edges.example: budget pushes closed over gold OA
edges.resolution_rule: favor mandate-compliant OA unless budget infeasible, then seek waivers/diamond

edges.why_related: review rigor pressures editorial speed/throughput
edges.example: double-blind adds time vs desk-fast venues
edges.resolution_rule: rigor dominates for high-stakes claims; set explicit SLA

edges.why_related: fast preprint dissemination pressures slower legitimacy vetting
edges.risk_of_conflict: posting before vetting spreads unvetted claims
edges.resolution_rule: disseminate as preprint but defer trust claims until vetting

edges.why_related: soundness-only scale pressures selectivity-based legitimacy judgments
edges.risk_of_conflict: megajournal scale read as low quality
edges.resolution_rule: vet by transparency/soundness criteria, not selectivity alone

edges.why_related: rights retention pressures venue/cost choices that demand transfer
edges.resolution_rule: retain deposit rights; use addendum before accepting transfer

edges.why_related: indexing and identifier/metadata work share discovery infrastructure
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating them as identical hides distinct checks

edges.why_related: a failed provenance judgment can trigger re-vetting of the venue
edges.resolution_rule: re-vet at most twice, then escalate to human review

edges.why_related: synthesis can surface gaps that trigger provenance revisit
edges.resolution_rule: revisit once per upstream change, then escalate

conflict_axes.trigger: budget pressure pushes toward a cheaper but less-open route
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: mandate-compliant openness dominates cost unless no affordable compliant option exists
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: no affordable mandate-compliant route is available
conflict_axes.example: a funder requires CC BY gold but only a costly hybrid venue fits the topic

conflict_axes.trigger: desire to disseminate fast competes with thorough legitimacy vetting
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: trust vetting dominates any claim of validated reliability; speed allowed only for clearly-labeled preprints
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a preprint is being cited as validated evidence
conflict_axes.example: a media outlet cites an un-vetted preprint as a confirmed finding

conflict_axes.trigger: deeper review competes with faster editorial decisions
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: rigor dominates for high-risk or high-impact claims; throughput optimization only for low-risk content
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a high-stakes clinical claim is under tight production deadline
conflict_axes.example: a fast-track decision skips a needed statistical review

conflict_axes.trigger: a prestige venue demands copyright transfer incompatible with retention
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: deposit-enabling rights dominate prestige when a mandate requires retained deposit rights
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a funder mandate conflicts with a venue copyright-transfer clause
conflict_axes.example: a top venue refuses a rights-retention addendum

conflict_axes.trigger: megajournal soundness-only review is judged by selectivity-based legitimacy criteria
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: form-aware trust criteria dominate selectivity heuristics for megajournals and overlay journals
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a sound megajournal is dismissed for low rejection rate
conflict_axes.example: an overlay journal judged by impact factor it lacks

conflict_axes.trigger: automated discovery/metadata pipelines outrun human integrity review
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: human review dominates for high-risk trust and irreversible decisions; automation handles low-risk discovery
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an automated index surfaces a retracted paper as valid
conflict_axes.example: a pipeline trusts a venue without human predatory screening

conflict_axes.trigger: FAIR open-data goals conflict with licensing or confidentiality restrictions
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: legal/ethical restriction dominates openness for sensitive data; otherwise openness dominates
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: sensitive participant data cannot be CC0-shared
conflict_axes.example: a license forbids the redistribution a FAIR mandate expects

conflict_axes.trigger: a widely cited preprint competes with the authoritative version of record
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the version of record dominates for formal citation; preprint citation requires explicit version labeling
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a preprint accrues citations that diverge from the published VoR
conflict_axes.example: two DOIs cause split citation counts

conflict_axes.trigger: funder mandates constrain an author preferred venue or license
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: binding mandate compliance dominates author venue/license preference
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an author prefers a non-compliant subscription journal
conflict_axes.example: a preferred CC BY-NC license violates a CC BY mandate

edge_cases.trigger: a dependency or evidence ref points to a missing id
edge_cases.example: PUB_REPORT depends on a deleted node id
edge_cases.detection_method: run reference-resolution check against node/source registries

edge_cases.trigger: node object omits a required schema field
edge_cases.detection_method: validate every node against the required node structure

edge_cases.trigger: a heuristic estimate is labeled observed without data
edge_cases.example: a trust score marked observed with no dataset
edge_cases.detection_method: scan metric_labels for observed/experimentally_validated without OBSERVED_DATA

edge_cases.trigger: a node bundles multiple unrelated decisions
edge_cases.example: ROUTE_SELECT also doing license and cost work
edge_cases.detection_method: check node scope_boundary for multiple decision objects

edge_cases.trigger: a high-risk node lacks acceptance tests
edge_cases.detection_method: flag nodes with risk_if_wrong>=0.80 and empty acceptance_tests

edge_cases.trigger: an artifact is hard-locked before validation/review gates pass
edge_cases.example: decision record hard-locked before provenance validated

edge_cases.trigger: a feedback loop revisits without a stop condition
a tradeoff is encoded as a dependency
edge_cases.example: cost/openness tradeoff modeled as a prerequisite
edge_cases.detection_method: scan dependency edges for negative-tension relations

edge_cases.trigger: a dependent node is ordered before its prerequisite
edge_cases.detection_method: verify priority_order respects dependency topological order

edge_cases.trigger: retraction status not propagated to indexes/citations
edge_cases.example: a retracted paper still trusted in synthesis

edge_cases.trigger: the wrong version is cited or deposited
edge_cases.example: preprint DOI deposited instead of permitted AAM

edge_cases.trigger: a template placeholder survives into the populated KB
edge_cases.example: a node example still reads as an unfilled template token
edge_cases.detection_method: scan output text for known placeholder tokens

workflow.objective: fix artifact type, audience, and find/disseminate intent
workflow.do_first_because: scope stabilizes all downstream route, review, and trust decisions

workflow.objective: choose OA route and quantify cost
workflow.do_first_because: route and cost are high-coupling foundations that gate venue, license, and compliance

workflow.objective: select review model and venue form
workflow.do_first_because: review model defines the editorial workflow and feeds provenance

workflow.objective: set license, rights retention, and deposit plan
workflow.do_first_because: rights are high-irreversibility; signing away copyright can permanently block compliant deposit
preprint/data/authorship can proceed in parallel with rights once route is fixed

workflow.objective: run editorial production and resolve version lineage
workflow.do_first_because: version lineage must be resolved before identifiers, indexing, and provenance
PIDs and indexing make the artifact machine-retrievable and anchor provenance

workflow.objective: vet venue legitimacy and check post-publication status
workflow.do_first_because: legitimacy and retraction status are high-risk trust signals that gate provenance

workflow.objective: synthesize all signals into a provenance/trust judgment
workflow.do_first_because: provenance is the highest-coupling trust node and must follow all signal collection

workflow.objective: verify mandates and compile the auditable decision record
workflow.do_first_because: final synthesis must come last so no upstream decision is locked before validation and review

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk trust decision is under time pressure
dominance_rules.rule: risk-if-wrong dominates speed for high-risk nodes
dominance_rules.required_action: slow down and run acceptance tests
dominance_rules.example: do not rush a PROVENANCE judgment to meet a deadline

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node lacks an unmet prerequisite
dominance_rules.example: PUB_REPORT cannot precede PROVENANCE even if more valuable

dominance_rules.trigger: a numeric score is precise but its evidence label is wrong
dominance_rules.rule: correct evidence label dominates numeric precision
dominance_rules.required_action: fix the label before trusting the number
dominance_rules.example: a 0.87 trust score labeled observed without data must be relabeled heuristic

dominance_rules.trigger: an artifact is ready to lock but QA is incomplete
dominance_rules.example: do not hard-lock the decision record before compliance and traceability gates pass

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible decision is queued for automation
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation above risk/irreversibility thresholds
dominance_rules.example: a retraction-status trust call is escalated, not auto-decided

dominance_rules.trigger: adding more nodes threatens schema stability
dominance_rules.rule: schema stability dominates raw population count
dominance_rules.example: stop adding venue-form nodes until the node structure is consistent

dominance_rules.trigger: valid JSON conflicts with richer prose
dominance_rules.required_action: trim prose to preserve valid JSON
dominance_rules.example: shorten an example rather than break JSON with an unescaped quote

dominance_rules.trigger: a claim exceeds its source grounding
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade or remove the unsupported claim
dominance_rules.example: an observed-impact claim with no dataset is downgraded to heuristic

dominance_rules.trigger: a locally optimal step risks downstream rework
dominance_rules.example: resolve version lineage before assigning DOIs to avoid re-registration

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient ordering would create a dependency cycle
dominance_rules.rule: acyclic dependency structure dominates convenient sequencing
dominance_rules.required_action: convert the weaker edge to sequence/feedback
dominance_rules.example: the provenance<->vetting relation is split into dependency plus bounded feedback

anti_rework_rules.rationale: scope built on unresolved inputs causes full rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: scope locked while artifact type still ambiguous
anti_rework_rules.example: do not lock PUB_SCOPE before artifact type is confirmed

anti_rework_rules.rule: define competency questions before populating nodes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: nodes without CQ coverage drift from purpose
anti_rework_rules.example: every major node maps to at least one CQ before population

anti_rework_rules.rule: build source registry before assigning evidence labels
anti_rework_rules.example: SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR exists before any heuristic label is used

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix route before venue, license, and compliance
anti_rework_rules.rationale: downstream choices depend on the route
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: license chosen before route is known
anti_rework_rules.example: license and APC analysis wait for ROUTE_SELECT

anti_rework_rules.rule: decide rights retention before signing any agreement
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: agreement signed before retention strategy set
anti_rework_rules.example: add an author addendum before accepting a transfer clause

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve version lineage before assigning identifiers
anti_rework_rules.rationale: PIDs on the wrong version corrupt provenance
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: DOI registered before version map exists
anti_rework_rules.example: register the VoR DOI only after lineage is closed

anti_rework_rules.rule: collect all trust signals before provenance synthesis
anti_rework_rules.rationale: trust on partial signals is unsafe
anti_rework_rules.example: VENUE_VET, VERSION_CTRL, and RETRACT_CORR finish before PROVENANCE

anti_rework_rules.rule: run acceptance tests before hard lock
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: hard_lock set with failing acceptance tests
anti_rework_rules.example: the decision record stays draft until all gates pass

anti_rework_rules.rule: require human review before irreversible decisions
anti_rework_rules.example: rights transfer and retraction trust calls require human sign-off

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete traceability matrix before hard lock
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: decision record locked without trace links
anti_rework_rules.example: every decision in the record links to its evidence before lock

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and downstream impact

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling node

iteration_protocol.stop_condition: validation passes or only warnings remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: risk above threshold or unresolved high-risk defect
only low-risk defects remain below tolerance

test_cases.input_summary: single article needing a route and license decision
evaluate trust of a found preprint with a possible retraction
funder mandate conflicts with preferred venue license
